$comment: Machine-readable applicability metadata for the rule modules.
The Markdown module documents remain canonical: this file records WHEN a module or rule applies,
never WHAT it says. Nothing here generates documentation.
Workflows consult this to decide skip/apply; the reasoning behind a finding always cites the module text.
Keep in sync with the module headers — review-rules/workflow-contract.md C-3.
"workflows" lists the workflows that LOAD this file into a prompt — not the workflows whose
findings its rules can reach. The distinction decides digests: /code-review-fast loads fast.md
and no numbered module, so `fast` belongs on fast.md's entry alone even though the digest
compresses all of them. That link is recorded in fast.md's own notes and enforced by the
validator's fast-sync check; it does not belong here. Read the wrong way, this field silently
misreports what a workflow costs and what a workflow gates — both drifted before it said so.
$profileComment: Each profile carries the signals that establish it, so a skip decision rests on something found
rather than on an impression. A leaf signal is one of: dependency (package.json dependencies or
devDependencies, any workspace), file (glob), content (string, with 'in' naming where to look),
dirs (with an integer 'min' — how many of them must exist), profile (this profile is implied by
detect: "declared" means the profile cannot be read off the tree and must come from the user or
project config. Its 'hints' justify asking — they never establish the profile.
A false negative costs as much as a false positive: a module skipped because its profile went
undetected reads as a module with no findings.

react.description: Always true for this plugin — every module assumes a React codebase.

fsd.cautions: Requiring all six layers false-negatives real FSD projects — widgets and pages are commonly absent. Two matches are not evidence either: any project can have shared/ and features/ without the layering the module checks.

tailwind.cautions: Tailwind 4 moves configuration into CSS and ships no tailwind.config file, so a config-file-only check skips 11-styling.md on every v4 project. The dependency and the CSS entry point are the signals that survive both versions.

rsc.description: React Server Components: 'use client' boundaries inside an RSC-capable framework.

any.notes: top-of-file directive, single or double quoted

rsc.cautions: 'use server' alone marks a Server Function, not an RSC render tree — it is server-code evidence, not rsc evidence. Next.js with only pages/ is not RSC either.

ssr.description: Server-side rendering or static generation in use (includes RSC).
ssr.cautions: hydrateRoot is the client half of SSR — a project calling createRoot only is not server-rendered no matter what framework is installed.

three.description: Three.js / React Three Fiber / WebGL in the codebase.

tanstack-query.description: TanStack Query (React Query) used for server state.
tanstack-query.cautions: react-query is the pre-v4 package name; a project still on it has the same query keys and invalidation to review.

server-code.description: Server-side code reviewed in this repository (Electron main, BFF, route handlers, Server Functions).
server-code.cautions: The question is whether server code is reviewed *in this repository*, not whether the app talks to a server. A frontend calling someone else's API does not hold this profile.

contract-provider.description: This repository provides a contract consumed by others (API, IPC, published package).
contract-provider.declaredBy: The user, or project configuration. Whether anything outside this repository consumes the contract is a fact about the outside world and cannot be read off the tree — infer it and 16-5..16-7 fire on a type that is private to this repo.
hints: package.json without "private": true, carrying exports or bin
ipcMain.handle channels consumed by a separately released renderer
contract-provider.hintsNote: Hints justify asking the user. They never establish the profile on their own.
